overall: On reconsideration, the AG corrected factual errors about the regulations but kept its findings: the Oct 14 notice lacked access info until the day before and the gate-access item was too vague; repairs discussion and roll-call issue were not violations or declined.

allegations.summary: Notice for an October 14 remote meeting lacked public access instructions until it was amended less than 24 hours before the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Board’s notice for the October 14 meeting did not meet the requirements of the Open Meeting Law, as the notice did not contain the “place of the meeting” 48 hours in advance of the meeting.

allegations.summary: The notice item 'Rules and Regulations' with sub-item 'Gate Access at Reservation' was not specific enough about the hunting-access topic discussed.
allegations.key_passage: The Board’s notice was insufficiently specific to advise the public that the Board was contemplating granting gate access to the Reservation specifically to hunters.

allegations.summary: Discussion of repairs to inspection towers, gatehouses and a screenhouse under the 'other potential matters' item allegedly was not noticed.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find no violation with respect to the discussion of repairs, as the topic was not anticipated by the Chair 48 hours in advance of the meeting.

allegations.summary: During a roll call vote, two members allegedly voted 'here' instead of 'yes' or 'no'.
allegations.key_passage: We note that, even if true, this allegation would not constitute a violation of G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Within 30 days of receipt, re-hold a discussion of all topics discussed at the October 14 meeting, including re-voting any votes taken, at a properly posted future meeting, if not already done.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
